facts: In 2 N mixed acids (ranging from 2 N HNO3 to 2 N H2SO4), the behavior of Type 304 reflects its immunity to nitric acid and susceptibility to sulfuric acid.

NBS Circular 592 reports that stainless steels were resistant to fuming nitric acid, but that this resistance decreased with increasing temperature up to 160°F; the rate of erosive-corrosive attack in fuming nitric acid decreased with increased rate of flow.

In sulfuric acid, Kiefer and Renshaw reported that molybdenum-bearing types 316 and 317 were the most resistant at low temperatures, but that at about 150°F all of the stainless steels corrode in practically all concentrations of sulfuric acid (up to 95 percent).
Roach and Hall reported that molybdenum-bearing stainless steels were useful at room temperature in sulfuric acid concentrations below 15 percent and above 85 percent.
